metadata.description: An allocatable range of IP addresses that IPAddress records are carved from, so allocation ownership is expressible: which addresses are in play, who holds each, whether the pool is exhausted. A Base by the Base test (CLS-002): RFC 8344 and DHCP pool semantics abstract over every allocatable range, so a pool of a given prefix and ranges is fillable by any IPAM or DHCP provider. The same pool pattern as StoragePool and Volume: the carved record depends on its pool. Distinct from DHCPScope (the service-side configuration) and IPAddress (one consumed address).

zone.description: What kind of network this is — a governed network-zone term, for placement only (common-elements.schema.json `network_zone_ref`).

tier.description: How good this network is — a governed network_tier floor the provider reports (common-elements.schema.json `network_tier_ref`).

prefix.description: The subnet the pool draws from, in CIDR.

ranges.description: The allocatable ranges within the prefix. Absent means the whole prefix minus exclusions.

allocation_mode.description: How addresses leave the pool: `dynamic` (leased on request), `static` (reservations bound ahead of time), `mixed`. Aligns with `allocation` on the carved IPAddress.

exclusions.description: Addresses withheld from allocation (gateway, broadcast, known statics); never carved even inside a range.

total_addresses.description: DERIVED — computed from the pool's declared ranges (compute-never-store; a stored copy could disagree with the arithmetic). Count of allocatable addresses (ranges minus exclusions), once Realized.

allocated_count.description: DERIVED — a count of the IPAddress records allocated_from this pool; those records are the source (compute-never-store). Addresses currently allocated from this pool.

free_count.description: DERIVED — total_addresses minus allocated_count, both themselves derived; never stored independently. Remaining allocatable addresses.

exhausted.description: True when free_count == 0 — the pool-exhaustion signal capacity/placement and quota policies read.

relationships.name: subnet
relationships.description: The L3 network these ranges carve up. Added 2026-08-10 with Subnet: a pool is an ALLOCATION surface (which addresses may be handed out), never the network itself (what the network is, where its gateway is). Before the subnet class existed this pool's own `prefix` was standing in for both, which conflated the two.

relationships.name: network
relationships.description: The network segment this pool serves. A pool is scoped to one L2/L3 segment (VirtualNetwork/VLAN); addresses carved from it are reachable on that segment.

adopts.role: allocatable-range shape: a pool is one or more contiguous address ranges within a subnet from which addresses are handed out (dynamic) or reserved (static)
prefix + ip_family shape reused from IPAddress (same family, DCM ADR-023)

context.purpose: Makes an allocatable IP range a first-class record so allocation ownership and exhaustion are visible facts.
context.plain_description: A range of addresses that individual address records are carved from: the required subnet `prefix` (CIDR), the allocatable `ranges` inside it (start/end pairs — this allocation-side name differs from a DHCP scope's `pools` by design), `exclusions` (gateway, broadcast, known statics), and how addresses leave it — `allocation_mode`: `dynamic` (leased), `static` (reserved ahead of time), or `mixed`. Once realized it reports totals — allocated, free, exhausted — the signal capacity and placement policies read before asking for another address. Same pattern as a storage pool feeding datasets: the pool is the source, the carved record depends on it.
use_when: You need to know which addresses are in play, who holds each, and when a range is close to exhausted.
You need address allocation scoped to the one network segment the pool serves.
not_for: Service-side DHCP config for the subnet (options, lease time) — DHCPScope; the pool is intent-side inventory. The range overlap between the two is deliberate and documented on both.
A single address — IPAddress, carved from this pool.
works_with: IPAddress — the records carved from the pool (allocated_from).
VirtualNetwork — the segment the pool serves.
DHCPScope — the service-side projection of the same subnet.
